title: Intellect-only party: whole form of faith resides in mind assent
source_text: III. Illi ergo Theologi censent propriam fidei sedem esse solum hominis intellectum, & fidem, secundum totam formam & essentiam in solo intellectu esse & residere. Quippe integram fidei naturam constituunt in apprehensione veritatis coelestis a Deo revelatae, & in judicio atque assensu quodam qui circa eandem veritatem versatur. Nec alium proprium fidei actum agnoscunt, quam Verbum Dei nosse, eique, ut par est, credere atque assentiri, quae duo ad intellectum, non ad ullam aliam facultatem, pertinent.
pass_a_gloss: Those theologians therefore judge that the proper seat of faith is man's intellect alone, and that faith according to its whole form and essence is and resides in the intellect alone. For they constitute the entire nature of faith in the apprehension of heavenly truth revealed by God, and in a certain judgment and assent that turns about that same truth. Nor do they acknowledge any other proper act of faith than to know God's Word and, as is fitting, to believe and assent to it — which two belong to the intellect, not to any other faculty.
pass_b_english: For this party the whole essence of faith sits in intellect alone.
Proper acts: know the Word and assent — both intellective, none other.
